gen-dafont-quantum-gf-noto-sans-bhaiksuk: Loose, spacious, tech-flavored lettering up top, with Quantum drawing every stroke without a hint of thickening. Noto Sans Bhaiksuki follows with plump, tightly coiled lowercase and open mouths, so a long page of text stays easy going.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-noto-sans-brahmi: Thin, drawn-straight and generously spaced: that is Quantum, with its stroke edges running parallel around every curve. Noto Sans Brahmi has a high mean line and curves left open at the ends, which would keep paragraphs feeling light and current.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-noto-sans-buhid: Every glyph in Quantum looks traced with a single pen tip, loosely spaced and clean, against a body that has some modulation. Noto Sans Buhid has a high x-height and gaps at the curve ends, so lengthy text breathes.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-noto-sans-carian: Quantum has a pipe-cleaner feel, bent into loose, open letters with short ascenders and lots of room between them. And if it were shrunk down, Noto Sans Carian's terminals, which stay apart like scissor blades, would carry the page better.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-noto-sans-chakma: Quantum keeps one uninterrupted line width on every letter, spaced loosely, with its ascenders cut short and its mouths open. Big and brief is where it earns its keep.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-noto-sans-cham: A pen line that never changes width runs through Quantum, giving it a spacious, tech-minded look. Noto Sans Cham brings tall, rounded lowercase and open c forms, and that soft roundness is the strongest thing the two share.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-noto-sans-cherokee: Quantum looks like the single-width trail of a rolling-ball pen, loosely spaced, with ascenders cut unusually short. Noto Sans Cherokee sets a tall band of letters under small stalks, and its e opens wide.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-noto-sans-chorasmi: Noto Sans Chorasmian is the body here, big in x-height with short ascenders. Next to Quantum's hairline-free, shadow-free strokes and loose spacing, its curves that stop short of closing make the strongest quality: both feel open.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-noto-sans-cuneifor: Open-eyed e shapes and a lowercase puffed like inflated glass beads make Noto Sans Cuneiform read friendly and fresh. Quantum, drawn with a drafting pen's constant nib, earns its keep at big, short sizes.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-noto-sans-deseret: Flat, loose and contrast-free, Quantum looks drawn rather than set. It excels at spare, large lettering, while Noto Sans Deseret, wide-looking with squat ascenders and open apertures, does the work of being legible.
